questions.q: As he left Canada, what two pieces of advice did the author give the young audience?
options: Earn well, and give generously
Not quite. The article says: Make God your greatest concern, and be friendly towards all human beings.
Study science, and avoid politics
Not quite. The article says: Make God your greatest concern, and be friendly towards all human beings.
Make God your greatest concern, and be friendly towards all human beings
Yes. A short message, warmly received.
Travel widely, and write often
Not quite. The article says: Make God your greatest concern, and be friendly towards all human beings.
questions.rationale: “Firstly, make God your greatest concern. Secondly, behave in a friendly manner towards all human beings.”

questions.q: According to the article, what had kept people from investigating nature for so long?
options: The absence of writing
Not quite. The article says: Nature’s objects were held sacred and worshipped, so no one thought to study them.
Fear of long journeys
Not quite. The article says: Nature’s objects were held sacred and worshipped, so no one thought to study them.
Nature’s objects were held sacred and worshipped, so no one thought to study them
Right. The article says belief in one God removed this barrier.
A lack of instruments
Not quite. The article says: Nature’s objects were held sacred and worshipped, so no one thought to study them.
questions.rationale: “Holding the moon to be sacred was a major obstacle to even thinking of conquering it… Monotheism opened the doors of research and investigation by displacing nature from its sacred pedestal.”

questions.q: “The business of planting an orchard does not begin with the holding of an orchard conference.” What is the article saying about building a nation?
options: It is done by nurturing individuals one by one, from their early years
Yes. “Build the individual and you build the nation.”
It is done by a few great leaders
Not quite. The article says: It is done by nurturing individuals one by one, from their early years.
It happens by itself over time
Not quite. The article says: It is done by nurturing individuals one by one, from their early years.
It is done by passing resolutions
Not quite. The article says: It is done by nurturing individuals one by one, from their early years.
questions.rationale: “It begins by obtaining seedlings and providing every single one with such favourable conditions as will enable it to develop its potential.”

questions.article: The Advice of a Wise Man
questions.q: Which of these is part of Luqman’s advice to his son, as quoted from the Quran?
options: Walk modestly and lower your voice
Correct. God does not love the arrogant and boastful.
Keep away from people
Not quite. The article says: Walk modestly and lower your voice.
Speak loudly so that all may hear
Not quite. The article says: Walk modestly and lower your voice.
Seek wealth before all else
Not quite. The article says: Walk modestly and lower your voice.
questions.rationale: “Do not avert your face from people out of haughtiness and do not walk with pride on the earth… Walk modestly and lower your voice.”

questions.q: Alexander conquered much of the known world in ten years. What lesson does the article draw from his end?
options: Empires need better administrators
Not quite. The article says: He died as helpless as anyone, and his empire soon fell apart – death teaches what the living ignore.
He died as helpless as anyone, and his empire soon fell apart – death teaches what the living ignore
Well read. It spares neither high nor low.
Conquest is the surest road to fame
Not quite. The article says: He died as helpless as anyone, and his empire soon fell apart – death teaches what the living ignore.
Great men should name their heirs early
Not quite. The article says: He died as helpless as anyone, and his empire soon fell apart – death teaches what the living ignore.
questions.rationale: “He died in the ancient city of Babylon—as defenceless in the face of death as any poor man in his miserable hut.”

questions.q: The Prophet said, “I was sent to perfect the best in moral characteristics.” What does the article take from these words?
options: The message built on man’s inborn moral sense and aimed to raise him to his highest standard
Yes. It was not a wholly new morality.
Character matters less than belief
Not quite. The article says: The message built on man’s inborn moral sense and aimed to raise him to his highest standard.
Morality began only with his coming
Not quite. The article says: The message built on man’s inborn moral sense and aimed to raise him to his highest standard.
Earlier teachings were to be discarded
Not quite. The article says: The message built on man’s inborn moral sense and aimed to raise him to his highest standard.
questions.rationale: “While this points to the fact that the message he brought was not a new one, it also shows that the main purpose of the message was to make man live according to the highest moral standard.”

questions.q: How does the article define piety (taqwa)?
options: Withdrawing from ordinary life
Not quite. The article says: Being conscious of God and careful not to overstep His limits.
Knowing the scripture by heart
Not quite. The article says: Being conscious of God and careful not to overstep His limits.
Performing many rituals
Not quite. The article says: Being conscious of God and careful not to overstep His limits.
Being conscious of God and careful not to overstep His limits
Right. A defence against evil and temptation.
questions.rationale: “Piety means to be conscious of God and to be careful of not overstepping the limits set by Him.”

questions.q: What does the article say is the aim of informal education, and where is its centre?
options: Passing examinations; the school
Not quite. The article says: Building character and a sense of duty; the home.
Learning a trade; the workshop
Not quite. The article says: Building character and a sense of duty; the home.
Building character and a sense of duty; the home
Yes. Formal education prepares for a job.
Gaining rank; the office
Not quite. The article says: Building character and a sense of duty; the home.
questions.rationale: “Schools or colleges are centres of formal education, while homes are the centres for informal education… the focus of informal education is to develop quality character in people.”

questions.q: In the study the article describes, how did high achievers speak of their setbacks?
options: As matters best forgotten
Not quite. The article says: As false starts, never as failure – each one spurring greater resolve.
As false starts, never as failure – each one spurring greater resolve
Exactly. There was always another idea to try.
As the fault of others
Not quite. The article says: As false starts, never as failure – each one spurring greater resolve.
As proof they had chosen wrongly
Not quite. The article says: As false starts, never as failure – each one spurring greater resolve.
questions.rationale: “Many spoke of false starts but never of failure. Disappointment spawns greater resolve, growth or change.”

questions.q: Why does the article name peace, not freedom, as the greatest good (summum bonum)?
options: Peace is easier to achieve
Not quite. The article says: Peace never has a harmful result, whereas unchecked freedom can end in anarchy.
Freedom belongs only to rulers
Not quite. The article says: Peace never has a harmful result, whereas unchecked freedom can end in anarchy.
Freedom is of no value
Not quite. The article says: Peace never has a harmful result, whereas unchecked freedom can end in anarchy.
Peace never has a harmful result, whereas unchecked freedom can end in anarchy
Well reasoned. Peace is like the soil in which all else grows.
questions.rationale: “Summum bonum refers to the maximum use of something which does not have any negative results, while the unchecked use of freedom can result in anarchy.”
